profile.summary: PoET (Protein Evolutionary Transformer) is a generative protein language model that treats a whole protein family as one long sequence of related sequences. Given a set of homologous sequences for a protein of interest, it scores variants of that protein or generates new family members. The released code scores a list of variants against a multiple sequence alignment (MSA) of homologues and writes one fitness score per variant.

summary_quotes.text: we propose Protein Evolutionary Transformer (PoET), an autoregressive generative model of whole protein families that learns to generate sets of related proteins as sequences-of-sequences across tens of millions of natural protein sequence clusters.
PoET can be used as a retrieval-augmented language model to generate and score arbitrary modifications conditioned on any protein family of interest
Use the script `scripts/score.py` to obtain fitness scores for a list of protein variants given a MSA of homologs of the WT sequence.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PoET is a stack of Tiered Transformer decoder layers with causal self-attention. Each layer works in two phases: it first attends within each sequence, then attends across the whole set of sequences joined together. Tokens are modelled in order within a sequence, while the order of sequences in the set does not matter. Training used 29 million sets of homologous sequences, one set per UniRef50 (version 2103) sequence with its UniRef50 homologues found by Diamond. To score variants, PoET conditions on homologues retrieved for the wild-type sequence (the final method uses the ColabFold protocol) and averages the conditional log-likelihoods over 15 subsamples of those homologues.

quotes.text: The TieredTransformerDecoderLayer is composed of two phases.
full PoET model is a stack of these layers with causal self-attention.
we model tokens sequentially within sequences while attending between sequences order invariantly
Models were trained on 29 million sets of homologous sequences. Each set corresponds to a sequence in UniRef50 Version 2103, and contains all its homologs in UniRef50 found using Diamond [34].

Our final approach uses the ColabFold protocol [35] for retrieving homologs, and the final fitness prediction score is obtained by averaging the conditional log-likelihoods across subsamples of the full set of retreived homologous sequences
All combinations of these parameters are used, for a total of Nensemble = 15.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper trained 57M, 201M and 604M parameter models and chose the 201M version as the standard PoET model. The repository releases one checkpoint, poet.ckpt (403,195,613 bytes on Zenodo, record version 1.0.0, published 2023-11-01), which the README describes as about 400MB. The sources read do not state which of the three sizes this file is. A result should name the Zenodo record and the commit of the scoring code, and also the homologue set used, because PoET scores depend on the MSA it is given.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Autoregressive generative protein language model over sets of homologous sequences, used as a retrieval-augmented model for variant scoring and sequence generation.

quotes.text: an autoregressive generative model of whole protein families
PoET can be used as a retrieval-augmented language model

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer decoder built from TieredTransformerDecoderLayers: causal attention within each sequence, then causal attention over the concatenated set. The 201M model has 12 layers and hidden dimension 1024 (paper Table 3).

quotes.text: full PoET model is a stack of these layers with causal self-attention.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: An MSA of homologues of the wild-type sequence in a3m format and a FASTA file of variant sequences to score.

quotes.text: --msa_a3m_path <path to MSA of homologs of WT sequence>
--variants_fasta_path <path to fasta file containing variants to score>

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: One fitness score per variant, saved as a NumPy array; the model can also generate new sequences conditioned on a family.

quotes.text: --output_npy_path <path to output file where scores for each variant will be stored as a numpy array>
We also demonstrate PoET’s ability to controllably generate new protein sequences.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: 201M for the standard PoET model in the paper; 57M and 604M versions were also trained. The released poet.ckpt is not labelled with a size in the sources read.

quotes.text: We chose the 201M version as the standard PoET model.
we trained 57M, 201M, and 604M parameter models

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: 29 million sets of homologous sequences built from UniRef50 version 2103 with Diamond; sets with fewer than 10 homologues were removed and sets were sampled with inverse-count weighting.

quotes.text: Models were trained on 29 million sets of homologous sequences.
We removed any sets with fewer than 10 homologs.

facts.label: Known versions
facts.value: One public checkpoint: poet.ckpt in Zenodo record 10061322 (version 1.0.0). The paper also describes 57M and 604M models used in ablations; they are not in the Zenodo record.

quotes.text: "key": "poet.ckpt"

facts.label: Training cutoff
facts.value: UniRef50 version 2103 is the training database. No other cutoff date is given.

quotes.text: Each set corresponds to a sequence in UniRef50 Version 2103

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 8K tokens is the training context of the models compared in the architecture study; scoring subsamples use 6144, 12288 or 24576 tokens of homologues, and PoET generalised to about 61K tokens, the longest tested.

quotes.text: We trained both models with a context length of 8K for 500K steps.
total tokens (i.e. context length) in {6144, 12288, 24576}.
PoET generalizes to ~8x the training context length (61K), which is the longest we tested.

run_guide.summary: Build the PoET conda environment at a pinned commit, download the weights and score the bundled ProteinGym example assay.
prerequisites: mamba and conda-lock installed in the base environment, as the README requires.
An NVIDIA GPU; the model cannot run on CPU. The README says the script was tested on an A100 GPU with 40GB VRAM and suggests a lower --batch_size if memory runs out.
The weights are CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for academic use only.
